A 49-year-old female with diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia comes to your office reporting
fatigue and generalized weakness for two weeks. She has recently begun disease-modifying therapy
for newly diagnosed rheumatoid arthritis. The patient expresses feelings of guilt about being unable to
participate in sports activities with her children. Her review of systems reveals occasional bright red
blood on toilet paper. Laboratory results show: - Hemoglobin: 12 g/dL - Hematocrit: 36% - Leukocyte
count: 7,700/mm^3 with normal differential - Platelet count: 207,000/mm^3 - MCV: 110 fL What is the
most probable cause of her fatigue? Answer Choices: (A) Gastrointestinal bleed (B) Drug-induced
myelosuppression (C) Folate deficiency (D) Depression-related fatigue (E) Iron deficiency anemia (F)
Anemia of chronic disease (G) Early-stage myelodysplastic syndrome (H) Subclinical hypothyroidism
(I) Medication side effect (J) Vitamin B12 deficiency
 A. Folate deficiency
B. Early-stage myelodysplastic syndrome
C. Subclinical hypothyroidism
D. Depression-related fatigue
E. Medication side effect
F. Drug-induced myelosuppression
G. Gastrointestinal bleed
H. Iron deficiency anemia
I. Anemia of chronic disease
J. Vitamin B12 deficiency
